before.description: The A/C compressor can fail, particularly on vehicles in hot climates with heavy A/C use. Internal compressor failure can contaminate the A/C system. Clutch and bearing failures are also common.
before.solution: Replace A/C compressor assembly. If internal failure, flush entire system, replace condenser, receiver/drier, and expansion valve. Use quality replacement parts. Aftermarket compressors available at lower cost.

before.title: Front Radar / Forward Collision-Avoidance Warning Disabled by Sensor or Calibration Faults
before.description: Owners have reported the Forward Safety system, Smart Cruise Control, and related ADAS features becoming unavailable with warning messages such as front radar blocked or forward safety system disabled. In some cases the problem appears after minor front-end work, bumper cover replacement, windshield service, or without obvious damage, pointing to radar alignment, sensor contamination, bracket movement, or module faults. This is well documented through owner complaints and Hyundai service information covering ADAS inspection and calibration procedures.
before.solution: Inspect the front radar area for impact damage, loose mounting, water intrusion, debris, or non-OEM bumper/grille parts affecting radar transmission. Perform a full scan for ADAS faults and complete static/dynamic calibration per Hyundai procedure; replace the radar sensor or bracket if alignment cannot be achieved or internal faults are stored. After repairs, verify operation of FCA, SCC, and lane/driver-assist functions on a road test.

before.title: MDPS / Electronic Power Steering (EPS) sudden assist loss and steering lockup
before.description: The Motor-Driven Power Steering (MDPS) unit can fail, illuminating the EPS warning light and causing sudden loss of power assist or a steering wheel that becomes very tight/hard to turn - sometimes during low-speed maneuvers (parking, tight turns) and sometimes at highway speed (~35 mph). Owners report having to stop, shift to park, and restart the engine to clear the light, and that the wheel can briefly 'lock' or require very high effort. Root causes traced to the MDPS module/motor, wiring-harness connections, or the steering-angle sensor. Hyundai issued a warranty extension covering the MDPS/EPS unit for EPS-warning-light illumination on 2016-2017 model-year vehicles from 5yr/60,000 mi to 15yr/150,000 mi.
before.solution: Scan for MDPS-related codes and inspect the wiring harness/connectors and steering-angle sensor before condemning the unit; repairing a connection sometimes resolves it. A failed MDPS module is replaced. For 2016-2017 vehicles the MDPS/EPS unit is covered under the extended warranty (15yr/150,000 mi) when the EPS light illuminates - have it documented and repaired under that coverage.
symptoms: Sudden loss of power steering assist
Steering wheel very hard to turn or briefly locked
Loss of assist during tight low-speed turns or at ~35 mph
Light clears only after restarting the engine

before.title: P0011 — Intake Cam Over-Advanced from Failed Oil Control Valve (CVVT)
before.description: On the Sonata, P0011 (Intake Camshaft Timing Over-Advanced, Bank 1) is set when the CVVT phasing runs further advanced than commanded. The most common Sonata cause is a failed/clogged intake Oil Control Valve (OCV/VVT solenoid) — the CVVT system uses oil pressure metered by the OCV to phase the cam, so a sticking solenoid or contaminated oil passages drive the cam over-advanced. Low oil level, wrong viscosity, or dirty oil commonly cause or worsen it; a displaced timing chain is a more severe possibility. A useful field test is swapping the intake and exhaust OCVs (identical, one bolt each): if the code migrates to P0014, the moved OCV is the faulty part.
before.solution: Verify oil level, condition, and correct viscosity first — top up/change oil if degraded. Test the intake OCV (coil resistance ~6.8-8.0 ohms at 68°F) and swap intake/exhaust OCVs to confirm; replace the failed OCV. Clean the OCV oil-feed screen/passages. If timing components are displaced, inspect and correct the timing chain.

before.title: P0016 — Crank/Cam Correlation Fault from Stretched Timing Chain (Theta II 2.4L GDI)
before.description: On the 2010-2015 Sonata with the 2.4L Theta II GDI engine, P0016 (Crankshaft/Camshaft Position Correlation, Bank 1 Sensor A) most often signals a stretched timing chain or a worn/failing chain tensioner, letting the intake cam fall out of sync with the crank. Poor oil flow and soot/metal debris in these GDI engines accelerate chain stretch and guide wear — the same oil-starvation environment behind the engine's bearing-failure lawsuit. A faulty intake Oil Control Valve (OCV) can also set it. Left unaddressed, the chain can jump time and cause valve-to-piston contact and severe engine damage.
before.solution: Inspect the timing chain, guides, and tensioner; replace the chain kit (chain, tensioner, guides) if stretched. Verify oil level/quality and correct any oil-consumption problem feeding the wear. Test the intake OCV and replace if faulty. Check for open Theta II recalls/warranty extensions, as related engine repairs may be covered.
symptoms: Rattle/whine from front of engine at startup

before.title: P0128 — Engine Not Reaching Operating Temp from Stuck-Open Thermostat
before.description: On the Sonata (notably the 2015-2019 2.4L), P0128 sets when the ECM sees the engine failing to reach thermostat regulating temperature within the expected time. The overwhelmingly common cause is a thermostat stuck open — often within the plastic thermostat housing assembly, which becomes brittle and is sold as a unit with the thermostat and seal. The second most likely cause is a faulty engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor. A tell-tale sign is weak cabin heat, since coolant never fully warms.
before.solution: Confirm the engine is actually running cool (scan-tool ECT vs. gauge). Replace the thermostat / thermostat housing assembly; note the jiggle valve must be oriented at the top so trapped air bleeds out. Removing the battery and air intake box is typically needed for access. If the thermostat is fine, test/replace the ECT sensor. Refill and bleed the cooling system.
symptoms: Temp gauge reads low / slow to warm

before.title: P0171 — Bank 1 Lean from Intake Manifold Gasket Vacuum Leak / Stuck Purge Valve
before.description: On the Hyundai Sonata, P0171 (System Too Lean, Bank 1) is most commonly triggered by unmetered air entering downstream of the MAF sensor. The two dominant Sonata-specific sources are a leaking intake manifold gasket and a canister purge valve that sticks open. Because the MAF never counts this extra air, the ECM under-fuels and long-term fuel trims climb past the lean threshold. A dirty MAF hot-wire element is the third common contributor. On V6 Sonatas the upper intake plenum gasket is a known leak point; on the 2.4L four-cylinder a cracked PCV hose or brittle intake gasket is typical.
before.solution: Perform a smoke test of the intake to pinpoint the leak. Replace the intake manifold/plenum gasket if leaking; replace a stuck-open canister purge (solenoid) valve; clean or replace the MAF sensor; inspect and replace cracked PCV hoses. Clear codes and confirm fuel trims return to near zero after the repair.

Because the MAF never counts this extra air, the ECM under-fuels and long-term fuel trims climb past the lean threshold. A dirty MAF hot-wire element is the third common contributor. On V6 Sonatas the upper intake plenum gasket is a known leak point; on the 2.4L four-cylinder a cracked PCV hose or brittle intake gasket is typical.
proposal.solution: Perform a smoke test of the intake to pinpoint the leak. Replace the intake manifold/plenum gasket if leaking; replace a stuck-open canister purge (solenoid) valve; clean or replace the MAF sensor; inspect and replace cracked PCV hoses. Clear codes and confirm fuel trims return to near zero after the repair.

before.description: P0174 (System Too Lean, Bank 2) only applies to the V6 Sonata, since the four-cylinder has a single bank. A leak isolated to one bank is rarer than the whole-engine plenum leak.

Simultaneously address any common contributors: clean/replace the MAF, replace cracked PCV hoses, and verify fuel pressure. Reset trims and road-test to confirm both bank trims normalize.

before.title: P0420 — Bank 1 Catalytic Converter Failure from Theta II 2.4L GDI Oil Consumption
before.description: On the 2011-2019 Sonata with the 2.4L Theta II GDI engine, P0420 (Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold, Bank 1) is frequently a downstream symptom of the engine's well-documented excessive oil consumption. As worn rod bearings/rings let the engine burn oil, phosphorus and other contaminants coat and eventually melt the catalyst's honeycomb, killing its efficiency and setting P0420. Replacing only the converter without fixing the oil-burning root cause leads to rapid re-failure. This ties directly into Recall 132 (NHTSA 15V-568) for connecting-rod bearing wear and the KSDS software / extended 15yr-150k-mile short-block warranty.
before.solution: First diagnose and correct the underlying oil consumption — check eligibility under Recall 132/KSDS and the extended engine warranty; the short block may be replaced under warranty. Per Hyundai TSB (ECM update for related P0171/P0420 concerns), apply the ECM software update, then replace the failed catalytic converter only after the oil issue is resolved so the new cat does not fail again.
symptoms: Elevated oil consumption / low oil warnings

before.title: P0430 — Bank 2 Catalytic Converter Efficiency Failure (V6)
before.description: P0430 (Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold, Bank 2) applies only to the V6 Sonata, which has two catalyst banks. On the 2006-2010 Sonata 3.3L Lambda V6 the bank 2 warm-up catalytic converter degrades so the downstream O2 sensor tracks the upstream sensor too closely, indicating the cat can no longer store/convert oxygen efficiently. Age, high mileage, or upstream causes (an exhaust leak or a lazy/failing O2 sensor) accelerate it.
before.solution: Verify there is no exhaust leak and that both bank 2 O2 sensors are healthy (a failing rear sensor can mimic P0430). If the converter is confirmed inefficient, replace the bank 2 catalytic converter — replacing the O2 sensor alone sometimes clears it but usually the cat must be replaced.

before.title: P0442 — Small EVAP Leak from Gas Cap Seal or NVLD Sensor
before.description: On the Sonata, P0442 (small EVAP leak, ~0.020-0.060 in) most often comes from a simple sealing failure or the Natural Vacuum Leak Detection (NVLD) assembly. The gas cap O-ring hardens/cracks with age, and rust on the filler-neck sealing surface prevents a good seal. Hyundai has acknowledged (TSB 21-01-035H) that salt/marine environments contaminate the NVLD sensor, and Sonata Hybrid (2011-2015) is specifically prone to NVLD-driven small-leak codes in coastal areas. A canister purge valve that seals poorly can also produce a small leak.
before.solution: Start with the cheap items: inspect/replace the gas cap and clean the filler-neck sealing surface with a Scotch-Brite pad. Smoke-test the EVAP system to locate the leak. Replace the NVLD assembly if contaminated/faulty (Hyundai has issued an updated EVAP air-filter kit and NVLD replacement guidance for salt-contaminated units), and replace a leaking purge valve.

before.title: P0455 — Gross EVAP Leak from Loose/Failed Gas Cap or Stuck Purge Valve
before.description: P0455 (large/gross EVAP leak, ~0.040 in or larger) on the Sonata is most commonly a loose, missing, or failed gas cap, a canister purge valve stuck open (constant EVAP vacuum leak), or a faulty NVLD sensor — the same coastal salt-contamination pattern Hyundai has documented (TSB 21-01-035H) affecting the Sonata/Sonata Hybrid EVAP system. Larger leaks can also come from a cracked EVAP/vent hose or a damaged charcoal canister.
before.solution: Verify the gas cap is tight and its O-ring is intact; replace if degraded. Smoke-test to find the gross leak. Replace a stuck-open canister purge valve or a cracked EVAP line; replace the NVLD assembly if contaminated. Re-run the EVAP monitor to confirm the leak is sealed.
symptoms: Sometimes rough idle if purge valve stuck open

before.title: Panoramic sunroof wind-deflector detachment / glass shattering
before.description: On Sonatas equipped with the panoramic sunroof, the wind-deflector anchor plate can be insufficiently bonded; if the deflector partially detaches while the roof is open it can interfere with the closing panel and cause the glass sunroof panel to detach from its mounting tabs and fly off the vehicle. Hyundai recalled 62,811 2015-2016 Sonata (incl. Sonata Hybrid) under NHTSA recall 16V-726 (Campaign 152). Separately, Hyundai panoramic sunroofs across 2010-2016 models have a documented tendency to spontaneously shatter (owners describe a gunshot-like sound with glass falling into the cabin); a class-action settlement provided an extended 10-year/120,000-mile warranty for shattered-sunroof repairs.
before.solution: For the detachment defect, dealers apply a revised/stronger bonding to the wind deflector under recall 16V-726 (Campaign 152), free of charge - verify the recall is closed by VIN. For spontaneous glass shattering, repairs may be covered under the 10yr/120,000-mi class-action warranty extension; replacement of the laminated panoramic glass otherwise runs roughly $500-$1,500+ depending on parts and headliner damage.
symptoms: Sunroof wind deflector rattles or detaches when roof is open
Sunroof glass panel detaches/flies off the vehicle
Spontaneous shattering of the panoramic glass with a loud bang
Broken glass falling into the cabin

before.title: Theta II 2.0T/2.4L GDI connecting-rod bearing failure (knock, stall, fire)
before.description: The Theta II GDI engine (2.4L MPI/GDI and 2.0T) suffers premature connecting-rod bearing wear. NHTSA determined that metal debris left from crankshaft machining, plus uneven crankpin surface roughness, restricts oil flow to the rod bearings, raising bearing temperatures and causing premature wear. A worn bearing produces a metallic, cyclic knocking noise that increases with RPM; if driven further the bearing fails, the engine can seize and stall while in motion, and a fractured rod can puncture the block, letting oil reach hot surfaces and start an engine-compartment fire. This is the defect behind multiple recalls (Campaign 132 / NHTSA 15V-218 for 2011-2012 2.0T/2.4 GDI built at HMMA; Campaign 198 / NHTSA 20V-746 covering Sonata Hybrid and others), a $210M NHTSA civil penalty consent order, and a ~$1.3B class-action settlement covering roughly 3.9M Hyundai/Kia owners.
before.solution: Have the dealer perform the recall engine-inspection test (rod-bearing/Knock Sensor Detection System diagnostic). If bearing damage is found, the engine is replaced free under the campaign. All affected vehicles receive the KSDS software update that detects pre-failure knock and limits power. Settlement extends powertrain warranty to 15 years / 150,000 miles for rod-bearing failure (transferable to subsequent owners), with reimbursement for prior repairs. If you hear a metallic knock that rises with RPM or see the oil-pressure/check-engine light, stop driving and get it inspected immediately.
symptoms: Metallic cyclic knocking noise that increases with engine RPM
Check-engine light and/or oil-pressure warning lamp
Engine stall while driving / engine seizure
Knock at cold start or under light acceleration

before.title: Theta II GDI excessive oil consumption
before.description: Hyundai TSB 23-EM-008H provides inspection and repair guidance for gasoline-engine vehicles with oil-consumption concerns. Its engine and labor tables specifically include model-year 2011-2014 Sonata 2.4-liter GDI and 2.0-liter turbo-GDI applications and model-year 2015-2020 Sonata 2.4-liter GDI and 2.0-liter turbo-GDI applications. The bulletin states that all internal-combustion engines consume some oil in normal operation and does not assign one universal defect cause.
before.solution: Ask a Hyundai dealer to follow TSB 23-EM-008H and confirm coverage. After preliminary checks and repair of any leaks or other open issues, the procedure seals the serviced engine and measures oil use over a mileage-accumulation period. A result above 1,000 miles per quart passes; a result under 1,000 miles per quart proceeds to prior-approval review for combustion-chamber cleaning. Engine replacement is considered only after the cleaning and final retest remain outside specification and prior approval is obtained.
symptoms: Measured consumption under 1,000 miles per quart

before.title: Theta II Engine Seizure/Failure
before.description: The Theta II engine can seize due to metal debris blocking oil flow to connecting rod bearings. Hyundai issued recalls and extended warranties. Affected engines may need replacement.
before.solution: Check VIN for active recalls - Hyundai provides free engine replacement for affected vehicles. Install the knock sensor detection system (KSDS) software update that monitors for bearing wear. Change oil every 5,000 miles. If engine fails and under warranty, replacement is free. Out of warranty replacement: $4,000-8,000.
